mode: read-only semantic audit; only temp artifact writes
scope: Canonical public managed-cloud schedule/event/AGI Work execution chains plus actual Electron and retained Tauri distinction. Selected source ranges were semantically read; neither the entire source manifest nor every historical alternative was semantically read in this lane.

competitor_evidence.status: documented; primary page read by parent /root this turn, communicated to child; no observed UI
relevant_claims: Dot has own cloud computer; scheduled/in-progress/completed work; customizable behavior and persistent memory. Local computer permissions off by default, explicit allow/revoke. Pause/resume/reset.
Gradual eligible Pro and Business Premium rollout; Enterprise beta off by default; geographic/mobile/SMS limits apply.

competitor_evidence.status: documented primary web page; no observed UI
relevant_claims: Named bots with separate jobs/context/memory, persistent account shared cloud computer/browser/files, coordinated group chats/handoffs, recurring schedules and work after laptop closure.

competitor_evidence.status: documented primary announcement; no observed UI
relevant_claims: Own computer, filesystem/terminal/browser; goals and multitasking event/schedule background work, persistent memory/persona, selective proactive interruptions and structured approval.

implemented: Mounted /chat/schedules UI and authenticated, CSRF-protected create API with plan/workspace quotas. PostgreSQL leased/idempotent claim and run rows; cron/once/interval/rrule/event types, retry/missed-execution, URL conditions, project/memory source scope.
Runs execute in the server cron, independent of client/laptop; interrupted claims and approvals are reaped/persisted.
limitations: Vercel timer is every 15 minutes. Each cron invocation is capped at 60 seconds; individual executions are bounded to about 40 seconds, not the interactive durable workflow continuation mechanism. Approval checkpoint resumes are another 40 second route invocation.
Actual production deployment, CRON_SECRET, DB migrations, provider eligibility and cron delivery are unknown.

implemented: Signed generic connector callback reaches ingest, transactionally deduplicates/caps/debounces delivery and enqueues database-backed event-triggers.fire job. Registered background handler reaches the real scheduled executor.
Background cron drains every 5 minutes; queue policy fences leased attempts and retries/dead-letters failures. Approvals persist through the shared scheduled-run mechanism.
limitations: Implemented/source-reachable, not production runtime validated. Event queue executes approximately 45 second attempts; long tasks do not use interactive workflow continuation. Webhook signatures, watch subscriptions and infrastructure credentials must be configured.

evidence.why: actual schedule executor and retry outcome

implemented: Canonical AGI Work/tool-loop entry starts Workflow server execution, writes durable run/event/checkpoint data, attaches workflow id and offers journal reattachment. Default initial-turn switch is enabled unless explicitly off.

Workflow invocation checkpoints automatically continue; device presence is rechecked before remote steps. The server waits up to 60 minutes for an asleep host, then removes its tools and continues cloud work.
limitations: Conditional: an inline fallback on unavailable workflow, billing input, first-byte budget or operator switch is request scoped and loses detachability. Simple single-turn chat without the tool/work path is not covered by this finding.

Liveness tests exercise workflow mocks and source; no live browser disconnect/restart or deployed workflow platform was tested. Local file/computer/browser actions still require awake, paired authorized hardware.

evidence.why: actual initial workflow mount and fallback
AGI Work capability gate also enforced before the initial route start; do not infer a kill-switch bypass solely from durable fallback

implemented: Mounted /tasks uses shared TasksPage, authenticated managed-run client and active/needs-you/all/archived filters; conversation navigation, pause/resume/cancel and approvals use common run IDs.
Lifecycle approval/input/completion/failure emits durable account notification feed and mobile/browser push. Schedule completion/approval feeds are queued and can push/email.
limitations: Notification transport registration, OS permissions, delivery/retry latency and all six surface renderings were not live verified. The reviewed Web task inbox and schedules are separate routes, not one persistent bot conversation.

implemented: Account instruction/style settings and project personalization scopes reach the attended model. Managed memory is persistent, consent/policy scoped, and durable turn settlement invokes auto-memory write service.
Scheduled execution reads project context, account/project memories and optionally past chats with a context manifest.
limitations: The reviewed public execution owners are account/project/conversation/run/task, not a independently named bot with its own persona/memory. No independent bot/group-conversation handoff was established; other product paths remain unknown rather than inferred absent by names.

Scheduled context constructs its system prompt from project/memory/past-chat/capability/task directive and does not call the account custom-instructions builder. It also sets conversationId undefined; repeat scheduled runs do not share a bot-owned conversation/code notebook through this path.

implemented: Cloud code/filesystem execution has scoped persistent sandbox mapping and code contexts, keyed by tenant+user+conversation or code session. Local browser/computer steps can be handed to a paired device/caller.
limitations: The scoped sandbox mapping is not an account-wide always-shared cloud computer/browser filesystem and login profile. Mapping TTL is 24 hours. Scheduled runs have no conversation scope in their ProcessedRequest.

Public tool execution path hands caller-owned browser commands back to the caller, or schedules device-host tools; it does not establish a durable account cloud GUI browser. An alternative remote MCP provider could supply a browser, but that deployment/account configuration is unknown.

implemented: Tool permissions distinguish allow/ask/block, approval events carry arguments, and checkpoints persist before stream termination. Authenticated approval resumes verify checkpoint owner and re-read current tool permissions. Durable runs can pause, accept guidance/input and resume from another surface.
Unattended schedules pause on escalation, persist checkpoint/request and disable further occurrences pending decision; authorized CSRF-protected decision route claims/resumes them.
limitations: Provider-native hosted tools requiring a pause are withheld if they cannot be governed. Live concurrency/race behavior and irreversible-action coverage across all tools were not comprehensively exercised in this lane.

evidence.why: owner lock and persistent approval checkpoint

implemented: URL changes, JSON response field conditions and event source filters/debounce can suppress unnecessary executions. Cancelled condition-not-met runs produce no completion notice.
limitations: A completed run is always offered a generic completion notification subject to channel preferences; no content novelty/relevance decision reaches this notification path. This is a narrower control than Muse documented selective meaningful proactive interruptions.

The canonical public schedule directive asks the model to return results without questions. Structured tool approval works separately; an autonomous assistant’s judgment about asking useful follow-up questions is not established in this scheduler flow.

evidence.why: only cancelled suppression then preference gate

new_findings.known_flaw_search: No matching existing row found by schedule/skipped/billingStatus/false-success searches in current audit/registers/known-flaws.md; canonical register left untouched.
new_findings.title: Policy-refused scheduled runs are recorded and announced as successful
new_findings.trigger: A task has already been claimed, then evaluateManagedComputeAccess denies it (e.g. subscription inactive or workspace policy).
new_findings.effect: Provider work is skipped, but the run finalizer records success, emits a completion notice and marks an event-trigger delivery fired; task history shows success while the result text says skipped.

evidence.why: normal result return on policy denial
approval-only special case then unconditional success
existing test expects skipped normal return

reproduction.result: exit 0; actual unchanged finalizer function extracted/transpiled from SHA-bound source returns status success and announces success for a subscription_inactive result
reproduction.scope: Real function body, simulated DB/executor dependencies; not a live API/DB integration test.

evidence.why: native host mounts actual local/developer operations

public_electron.assessment: Default public desktop is Electron remote web shell plus native host bridge, so web durable execution is its cloud path. Native device operations require this Electron process/paired host to be available.

retained_internal_tauri.status: implemented internal source; not public Electron evidence

evidence.why: local SQLite scheduler initialization and process background loop

retained_internal_tauri.assessment: Internal Tauri has a separate local SQLite-backed background scheduler. It is mounted in the retained Tauri app, not public Electron cloud runtime, and a local process loop cannot demonstrate server execution with that machine off.

semantic_diff_review.review: Full diff inspected; adds resetOnLogout action to clear facts/sync state. This strengthens user-cache lifecycle, not autonomous agent persona/cloud computer features. No other currently distinct manifest variant matched the focused scheduler/event/cloud-run/memory/host/browser path set.
semantic_diff_review.limitations: Path filtering of supplied current manifest is a relevance screen, not semantic review of every satellite variant.

instrument_limits: Isolated Vitest with mocked provider/queue/workflow/DB dependencies; these results do not prove deployed durable survival, cron timeliness or notification delivery.
Executor unit tests hit test Neon URL parse errors on some unmocked entitlement reads and use caught fallbacks. Tests still passed. No actual production DB/API was used.
Actual finalizer extraction reproduction is separate and documents its simulated dependencies.
